sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 3.8% a year from $22.7 billion in FY2016 to $31.7 billion in FY2025 [F1][F9][F198], while operating income compounded at 5.8% [F199].
The window is a slow, regulated growth story with two step changes: revenue jumped 17.1% in FY2022 [D239] and operating margin rose 3.7pp in FY2023 [D293].
The FY2022 revenue step came from rate cases, favorable weather and volumes, partly offset by the Commercial Renewables impairment [P26], with EU&I income lifted by retail volumes and weather [P33].
FY2020 was the trough, with net income down 63.3% [D157] on coal-ash settlement impairment charges and pandemic-driven volume losses [P60].
Electric Utilities and Infrastructure supplied 90.9% of FY2025 revenue [D541] and contributed 3.6pp of the 5.6% revenue growth [D543][D358].
Within it, residential electric was the largest line at 43.3% of revenue [D774], contributing 2.8pp of growth [D776].
Gas Utilities and Infrastructure added 2.0pp in FY2025 [D566], with Piedmont Natural Gas revenue up 32.1% [D682].
Operating income grew 8.8% against 5.6% revenue growth [D359][D358], an incremental operating margin of 41.4% [D378].
Diluted EPS grew 10.5% [D362] slightly ahead of 9.8% net income growth [D360] despite a 0.6% share-count increase [D374].
Operating margin reached 27.2% in FY2025 [F28], a window high [D932] and 4.3pp above the 22.9% median [D933].
The FY2025 margin rose 0.8pp [D370] as revenue growth outpaced operating-cost growth by 0.3pp [D379], with D&A at 24.3% of revenue [D341].
Net margin of 15.7% [F47] sits below the 17.6% peer median [D952], partly because interest expense reached $3.6 billion [X63].
Interest expense rose on higher outstanding debt balances and interest rates [P10], and the effective tax rate was 11.2% [D345].
Operating cash flow of $12.3 billion was 2.48x net income in FY2025 [F77][D346], against a window median free-cash-flow/net-income ratio of -0.62x [D942].
Capex of $14.0 billion was 44.2% of revenue [F87][D342] and 1.82x D&A [D348], leaving free cash flow at -$1.7 billion [F97] and a -5.3% margin [D343].
Fuel undercollections from rising commodity costs increased borrowings to finance expenditures until recovery [P36], weighing on FY2022 operating cash flow of $5.9 billion [F74].
Net debt reached $89.6 billion in FY2025 [D352], or 282.3% of revenue [D353], versus a peer median of -228.4% [D954].
Cash of $245 million [F137] covers 0.1 years of the latest burn [D356], and the current ratio fell to 0.55x [F177].
Return on average equity was 9.7% [D357], below the 12.6% peer median [D956], with long-term debt up 6.5% a year [F210].
Duke Energy funds capital needs mainly from operations, debt and equity issuance [P8], and dividends paid $3.2 billion in FY2022 [X122].
The current ratio of 0.55x [F177] is below 1.0x and near the 0.53x window low [D943], reflecting heavy short-term debt of $7.1 billion [X160].
Free cash flow has run below 80% of net income for three years [R4], at -0.34x in FY2025 [D347], as capex outruns cash generation.
Net cash has fallen for nine straight years into net debt of $89.6 billion [R3][D352], a persistent leverage trend.
FY2021 operating expenses, pretax income and tax were later restated [R6][R7][R8], so FY2021 comparisons carry a data-quality caveat.
Watch whether operating margin holds above the 22.9% window median [D933] or slips toward the 19.7% low [D931] in the FY2026 10-K.
Watch free cash flow: a move back above the -5.8% median margin [D939] would signal capex relief, while a repeat of the -19.0% low [D937] would confirm the burn.
Watch the current ratio against the 0.53x window low [D943]; a further decline would intensify the liquidity flag.
